chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the person in Ihram whose nails grow long or one of them breaks and causes him harm. He (peace be upon him) said: 'He should not cut any of it if he can bear it. But if it causes him harm, let him cut it, and let him feed, in place of each nail, a handful of food.'

key_terms.إِحْرَام: Ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.كَفَّارَة: Expiation or compensation for a violation

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling and expiation for a person in Ihram cutting their nails due to harm?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the prohibition on clipping nails during Ihram is not absolute but contingent upon the principle of avoiding undue hardship (darar), allowing the Muhrim to trim nails if they cause pain or injury. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on balancing ritual purity with physical comfort, prescribing a specific kaffarah of feeding one handful of food for each nail trimmed as compensation for the minor violation.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Muawiya Bin Ammar who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the one in Ihraam prolonging his nails, or one of them breaks, so that harms him. Heasws said: ‘He cannot cut anything from these if he can. So if it was harming him, so let him cut these, and let him feed in place of each nail, a handful of food’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who is in the state of Ihram and his nails grow tall or break and it annoys him. He (the Imam) said, ‘He must not cut anything if he can; but if it upsets him, he can cut them and for every nail he must feed a handful of (one meal) food.’”
